title: Protocol for single-molecule pull-down of fluorescently tagged oligomers from cell lysates
protocol: Warm the slide to 20°C–25°C for 15 min.
Tear off a 10 cm strip of double-sided tape and place on a glass plate or other sterile surface.
Cut the tape into 6-8 10 cm-long strips using a clean razor blade.
Carefully remove the slide from the conical tube and place the PEGylated side face-up on a glass plate.
Mark the coverslip with a sharpie to denote the PEGylated or non-PEGylated side of the coverslip.
Lift a tape strip and apply the strip to the slide between each pair of drilled holes and along the outer edge of the first and final pair of holes.
Use a pipet tip to gently secure the tape onto the slide.
Remove the coverslip and place it on the taped slide.
Take Petri dish from incubator.
Set up the TIRF microscope for the single molecule pull-down experiment.
Turn the camera on.
Ensure that appropriate laser(s) are on.
Open IDL for single-molecule trace processing.
Decant or aspirate media from Petri dish and discard.
Rinse Petri dish with 1 mL ice cold 1X dPBS and discard.
Add 1 mL ice cold cell lysis buffer to Petri dish and incubate on ice.
Apply 30 μL neutravidin diluted in T50 buffer at a 20 μg/μL concentration to one channel within the slide and incubate for ∼2 min.
Apply 50 μL T50 buffer to rinse off unbound neutravidin.
Apply 30 μL biotin-conjugated GFP antibody at a 5 μg/mL concentration after diluting 1 mg/mL stock antibody in T50 buffer to the slide and incubate for ∼2 min.
Apply 50 μL T50 buffer to rinse off unbound antibody.
Place lysed cells in Petri dish into microcentrifuge tube and pipet several times to further lyse.
Prepare a dilution of cell lysis in T50 buffer.
Gently pipette diluted cell lysate to ensure minimal condensate disruption.
Apply 50 μL diluted cell lysate onto the slide and incubate for ∼2 min.
Apply 50 μL T50 buffer to rinse off unbound complexes.
Set up slide on TIRF microscope.
Apply water to the objective on the TIRF microscope.
Place the single-molecule slide on the objective with the coverslip facing down.
Clean the prism with 100% ethanol.
Apply 1 drop of immersion oil to the prism and attach the prism to the microscope so that the oil surface is touching the slide.
Adjust the beam alignment for TIRF imaging.
Optimize the gain, exposure time, laser intensity, and z-plane focus for imaging the single-molecule surface.
Acquire 6–10+ videos capturing 600 frames at 100 ms/frame acquisition speed in different fields of view at maximum laser intensity in the excitation channel corresponding to the tagged protein.
Pipette 50 μL of dilution reagent at desired concentration into the channel.
Incubate for ∼2–10 min.
Wash twice with 50 μL T50 buffer to remove unbound complexes from the slide.
Remove excess oil and water from the slide and microscope objective as needed.
Set up the slide on the TIRF microscope as previously described.
Obtain photobleaching steps of fluorescently-tagged proteins.
Acquire 6–10+ videos capturing 600 frames.
Set the frame acquisition speed to 100 ms/frame.
Choose different fields of view for imaging.
Use maximum laser intensity in the excitation channel corresponding to the tagged protein.
Maintain the same gain setting throughout imaging.
Keep the exposure time constant during imaging.
Use consistent laser intensity for all images.
Focus on the single-molecule surface at the same z-plane.
